title: Finite pushforward of a constructible module sheaf with finite geometric stalks
statement: Let Lambda be a commutative ring, X a Noetherian scheme, f:Y -> X a finite morphism, and F a sheaf of Lambda-modules on the small etale site of Y. Assume F is constructible in Scheme.IsConstructibleSheaf [def-constructible-constructible], and that every geometric stalk over a separably closed field is finite as a set [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Then f_*F [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is constructible as a Lambda-module sheaf. No Noetherian hypothesis on Lambda is assumed.

source.place: Constructibility of the middle term: finite abelian pushforward and finite-ring module refinement; generalized finite-stalk formulation by T2, using Stacks Tag 095R

proof.text: Choose a constructible module stratification of F. Every stratum is Noetherian and quasi-compact. Discard empty members of its etale constant-module covers; on each remaining member, the constant module is a geometric stalk of F and therefore finite. Select finitely many cover members on each of the finitely many strata. Intersect the annihilators of their finite constant modules. This ideal I kills every geometric stalk of F, hence F itself. Lambda/I embeds in the finite product of their endomorphism rings, hence is finite. For empty Y use I = Lambda. This is the finite-coefficient reduction; its proof is part of this new theorem, not assumed as a separate lemma.

Regard F as a sheaf of modules over the finite ring Lambda/I, with the same source stratification and constant values. Apply the module-underlying-sets theorem over this finite ring. The finite morphism is finitely presented because its target is Noetherian. Apply the finite abelian direct-image theorem over the Noetherian target to the underlying abelian sheaf. Forgetting commutes with direct image, which is precomposition with base change, so this gives a finite-set constructible stratification of f_*F. The source annihilator still kills every direct-image section.

On each finite-set constant stratum, locally constant maps between constant finite sets are trivialized by refining the etale cover for their finitely many input values. Apply this to addition, zero, and each scalar operation of the finite ring Lambda/I; intersect the finitely many covering sieves and use transitivity of the topology. The algebraic relations remain those of the original sheaf. The resulting constant finite Lambda/I-modules are finitely generated over Lambda too. Thus these refinements trivialize f_*F as a module sheaf, with finitely generated geometric stalks, giving the required original Scheme.IsConstructibleSheaf. Empty strata can be discarded and zero stalks are handled by the zero module.
